sources.title: Trump Places DOL's ESOP Proposals in Regulatory Moratorium
Congressional Bills S. 240, S. 283, and S. 2403 Signed into Law
BILLSTATUS S. 2403 (119th Congress), Retire through Ownership Act
S. 2403, Retire through Ownership Act (enrolled bill)

status_summary: EBSA's ESOP adequate-consideration proposal and prohibited transaction exemption of 2025-01-16 were withdrawn under the 2025-01-20 regulatory freeze and never published, and no reissued DOL ESOP valuation or fiduciary rule appears in the Federal Register through 2026-10-18. Congress instead passed S. 2403, the Retire through Ownership Act (Senate 2025-10-09, House 401 to 14 on 2026-09-16), which the President signed on 2026-10-15. The enrolled text amends ERISA section 3(18) so that an ESOP fiduciary may rely on an independent appraiser following Revenue Ruling 59-60 when determining adequate consideration for stock not traded on a national exchange, leaves DOL free to issue interpretive regulations without requiring them, and states that it does not modify fiduciary duties under section 404.

timeline.event: The Senate passed S. 2403, the Retire through Ownership Act (introduced 2025-07-23, reported by the HELP Committee 2025-09-11), with an amendment by unanimous consent.
The House passed S. 2403 under suspension of the rules, 401 to 14 (Roll no. 314); the bill was presented to the President on 2026-10-05.

The President signed S. 2403, the Retire through Ownership Act, which amends ERISA section 3(18) to let an ESOP fiduciary rely on an independent appraiser following Revenue Ruling 59-60 in determining adequate consideration for closely held stock; the Act permits but does not require DOL interpretive regulations.
